hero.headline: Every task gets its own Claude
hero.sub: Open a task and a session is already sitting next to it — scoped to that one document, there to maintain it rather than to build it. And when you do want it built, one orchestrator takes it the whole way.

shot.alt: A task open in the dashboard with the Task Manager panel pinned beside it, showing a ready session and Revise, Summarize, Split and Status actions
shot.caption: The task on the left, its own session on the right — Revise, Summarize, Split, Status.

blocks.title: Four things it does without being asked twice

items.title: Revise
items.text: Sharpen the Why and the acceptance criteria until they say something testable instead of something vague.

items.title: Summarize
items.text: Compress a task that grew a long tail of session logs back into the shape someone can read in ten seconds.

items.title: Split
items.text: A task holding two jobs becomes two tasks, with the criteria distributed to the right one.

items.title: Status
items.text: Reconcile what the document claims against what actually happened in the repo, and bump it.

blocks.title: It maintains the task. It does not implement it.
blocks.body: That separation is the whole point. The Task Manager session loads a skill that keeps it on documentation work, so it never quietly starts writing product code in the background. When you do want the work done, Delegate hands the task to a build session instead.

shot.alt: A task detail panel with its identity, workflow, timeline and ownership fields, and Task Manager and Delegate buttons in the header

blocks.title: The other half: goal-skill was rewritten end to end
lines: $ claude  →  /goal-skill  add rate limiting to the public API
plan        1 planner        · file-by-file, grounded in the real routes
review      2 lenses         · pragmatist + risk, in parallel  → SOLID
implement   1 builder        · forked from the planner's context
validate    test suite       · the method you agreed to  → PASS
✓ task updated, criteria ticked, progress logged

blocks.title: Why that run is cheaper and more honest

items.title: Builders fork and resume
items.text: An implementer no longer re-explores the codebase from zero on every pass. It forks the session that already read it, so a second round costs a second round — not a second exploration.

items.title: Review stays independent
items.text: Reviewers and validators are dispatched clean, every time. A judge that inherited the builder's context would be marking its own homework.

items.title: Ceremony scales to the goal
items.text: A one-file fix does not get a planning phase, two plan reviewers and a validation gate. A migration does.

blocks.title: Sleep stopped duplicating what it already knew
blocks.body: Consolidation now reconciles against the knowledge that exists instead of appending a second file on the same topic every cycle. And a minimized agent keeps running in the corner: the chip reports live state, including a goal run's progress, and clicking it brings the pane back.

shot.alt: The Sleep Cycle page showing an Alert state with debt, the last consolidation summary, work sessions and starred highlights — with two live agent chips docked in the corner
shot.caption: Sleep Cycle after a consolidation — and, bottom right, the dock keeping two sessions alive.

blocks.title: Hand a task over from the card itself
blocks.body: Delegate starts a build session straight from the board — no copying a slug into a terminal to get going. New projects got the same treatment: a repo can be cloned from GitHub inside the setup wizard instead of being a thing you go and do first.

shot.alt: The task board in Kanban view with To Do, In Progress, In Review and Completed columns of task cards carrying version and tag chips

blocks.text: A validation that is flaky or skipped counts as FAIL. The validator reports the command it ran and its output, so a green result is evidence rather than a claim.

closer.title: How to start one
closer.body: Open any task and hit Task Manager to maintain it, or Delegate to have it built. From a terminal, /goal-skill with the goal in your own words does the whole run.
